risk_free_assumption.applied: month by month, not as a window average
risk_free_assumption.note: The Indian 10-year moved between 5.98% and 8.18% over this window, so the rate is applied to each month separately. Using the window mean would misstate both ends.

return_path.cvar_note: CVaR is the average return of the worst 5% / 1% of months, not a floor. A -10% monthly CVaR means roughly one month in twenty lost about a tenth of the book; the single worst was -9.4%.

risk_adjusted.sharpe_basis: measured Indian 10-year G-Sec, applied month by month

selection_bias.annualisation: sqrt(12); the comparison itself is per-observation
selection_bias.note: The allocation search evaluates 21 grid points against 4 regime rules, but adjacent grid points produce correlated portfolios, so only 16 are treated as independent. The count does NOT include variations tried by hand before this code existed, which would widen the adjustment if they were known. The closed-form expected maximum runs about 44% above a direct simulation of the same situation, so it is conservative; a simulation-calibrated figure (0.7x) is reported alongside it and would give a less strict but not indefensible verdict.

sharpe.method: moving block bootstrap (i.i.d. resampling would ignore serial dependence)
sharpe.basis: moving-block bootstrap of the measured excess-return series

decision_protocol.signal_date: Last completed trading day of the signal month
decision_protocol.information_cutoff: All inputs must be available by this timestamp
